title: Page the VCF Operations 9.0 alert collection to completion in a stable order

verification.network: loopback only; each scenario starts .protected/mock_vcf_ops.py on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port and no VMware endpoint is contacted
requirements: the VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops PowerShell module installed by the environment
verification.notes: run_tests.sh runs .protected/verify.py, which drives six scenarios. Each starts the contract-pinned loopback mock, calls Get-VcfOpsAlertInventory once through .protected/invoke-inventory.ps1, then asserts the emitted objects against .protected/fixtures/alerts.json and asserts the exact wire shape of every recorded request: the operation sequence, method, path, query keys and their order, repeated array keys, the absence of unset optional parameters, the Authorization and Accept headers, the issuing User-Agent, and that the session token is released even when a page request fails.

source_basis.not_derived_from: the 9.1.0.0 revision of the same file at commit 3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26

scenario: A VCF Operations 9.0 alert inventory is assembled by walking the paginated getAlerts collection from page 0 until pageInfo.totalCount is reached, then emitting every record in one deterministic order, with the session token acquired before the walk and released after it even when a page fails.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact wire shape: 0-based consecutive pages at a constant pageSize, resourceId repeated once per value, every unset optional query parameter absent rather than blank, and every page request issued by VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops rather than hand-rolled HTTP.
prompt:
Implement `Get-VcfOpsAlertInventory` in `src/VcfOpsAlertInventory/VcfOpsAlertInventory.psm1`, the one function a VCF Operations 9.0 alert inventory module exports. The function body is a `NotImplementedException`; the parameter block, the help and the manifest are already correct and must not change. Edit no other file and add no dependency.

The environment installs the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf` PowerCLI family, of which `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` covers VCF Operations. It is the supported client for these operations and the module manifest already requires it, so drive every call through its cmdlets. Do not vendor an SDK and do not reach for `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `curl` or `HttpClient`: the appliance records the `User-Agent` of every request, and each page request must come from the SDK.

`docs/contract.json` is the wire contract. It was derived from `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-openapi.json` at tag `9.0.0.0` of VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, and `docs/official_sources.json` records that spec path, the tag's commit sha and each operationId the contract names. Use exactly the four operations it names and call no other route: `acquireToken`, `getCurrentVersionOfServer`, `getAlerts` and `releaseToken`. Read the contract's `pagination` and `client` sections before writing the pager.

Open a session, walk the collection, then close the session. `acquireToken` runs once at the start and `releaseToken` once at the end; `getCurrentVersionOfServer` is the connect handshake and belongs before the first page. Every page request must be answered before `releaseToken`, and the token must be released even when the walk fails part way through, so a failed page must not leak the session.

Retrieve the collection completely. Paging starts at page 0 and walks consecutive ascending page numbers, sending the caller's `-PageSize` unchanged on every request. Stop when the records already retrieved reach `pageInfo.totalCount`, or when a page comes back with an empty `alerts` array. Do not treat the `links` array as a termination signal: a link with `rel` `NEXT` is present on every page including the last, so following `NEXT` until it disappears never terminates. Reading one extra empty page to confirm the end is acceptable; stopping early is not.

Honor the exact query shape. Each `getAlerts` request is a bodyless `GET` that sends no `Content-Type`, sends `Accept: application/json`, and carries the acquired token in the `Authorization` header using the prefix the contract records. `page` and `pageSize` appear exactly once each on every request. `id` and `resourceId` are optional arrays: send `resourceId` only when the caller supplied `-ResourceId`, repeating the key once per value in the order given rather than joining the values with commas, and never send `id` at all. An optional parameter the caller did not set is absent from the query string; it is never sent with an empty value. `-AuthSource` is likewise optional, and when it is supplied the acquired session must be authenticated against that named source.

Emit one object per alert, ordered by `StartTimeUTC` ascending and then by `AlertId` ascending compared ordinally. The collection is served in no guaranteed order, within a page or across pages, so impose the order yourself; timestamps repeat across alerts, so the `AlertId` tie-break decides those. Each emitted object carries exactly these properties in this order: `AlertId`, `ResourceId`, `AlertLevel`, `Status`, `StartTimeUTC`, `UpdateTimeUTC`, `AlertDefinitionName`. The two time properties are integers, the rest are strings. Emit nothing else, and when `-ResourceId` filters the inventory, emit no alert belonging to another resource.

A page the appliance refuses must abort the inventory. Surface it as a terminating error rather than returning a short collection, and request no further page after the failure.

Run `./run_tests.sh`. The protected verifier starts the shipped loopback mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port once per scenario and reads its request log. The mock builds its route table from `docs/contract.json`, so it serves only the four operations the contract names and records anything else as an off-contract call. Verification covers an unfiltered walk at three page sizes, a walk filtered to two resources, a named auth source, and a page that fails mid-collection; it asserts the emitted objects and the exact request sequence, method, path, query keys and their order, headers, issuing client, and the omission of every unset optional parameter. The verifier contacts no live VMware endpoint.
